title: Limit order book matching engine
statement: Process a stream of operations on one instrument: [0, id, price, qty] limit buy, [1, id, price, qty] limit sell, [2, id] cancel (ignore unknown or already-filled ids). An incoming order trades against the best opposite resting orders while prices cross (buy price ≥ ask, sell price ≤ bid), at the resting order's price, best price first and earlier orders first at equal prices (price-time priority). Any remainder rests in the book. Return the trades as [buy_id, sell_id, price, qty] in execution order.
hints: Bids: best = highest price, then earliest. Asks: lowest price, then earliest. A heap per side keyed by (price, arrival).
Cancels: don't search the heap; mark the order dead and skip it when it reaches the top (lazy deletion).
complexity: O(log n) per order (amortised, with lazy cancels)

solution.explanation: Model each side as a priority queue keyed by (price, arrival sequence): price priority, then time priority. Cancelling from the middle of a heap is the trap; lazy deletion (a live-orders map, dead orders discarded when they surface) keeps everything O(log n). Real engines use a price-level map (price → FIFO queue of orders) plus an id → order map, so that cancel is O(1) and the best level is cached: say this in the interview, and explain why (cancels outnumber trades many times over in real markets).
solution.python:
import heapq

def match_orders(ops):
    """ops: [0, id, price, qty] limit buy; [1, id, price, qty] limit sell; [2, id] cancel.
    Price-time priority; trades execute at the resting order's price.
    Returns trades [buy_id, sell_id, price, qty] in execution order."""
    bids, asks = [], []            # heaps: (-price, seq, id) and (price, seq, id)
    live = {}                      # id -> [side, price, remaining]
    trades = []; seq = 0
    for op in ops:
        if op[0] == 2:
            if op[1] in live: live[op[1]][2] = 0      # lazy cancel
            continue
        side, oid, px, qty = op; seq += 1
        book, opp = (bids, asks) if side == 0 else (asks, bids)
        while qty and opp:
            key, _, rid = opp[0]
            rest = live.get(rid)
            if not rest or rest[2] == 0: heapq.heappop(opp); live.pop(rid, None); continue
            rpx = key if side == 0 else -key
            if (side == 0 and rpx > px) or (side == 1 and rpx < px): break
            q = min(qty, rest[2]); qty -= q; rest[2] -= q
            trades.append([oid, rid, rpx, q] if side == 0 else [rid, oid, rpx, q])
            if rest[2] == 0: heapq.heappop(opp); live.pop(rid, None)
        if qty:
            live[oid] = [side, px, qty]
            heapq.heappush(book, (-px, seq, oid) if side == 0 else (px, seq, oid))
    return trades
